exam: What is the first step in managing a preterm infant at risk of ROP? — Maintain SpO2 90–95% and treat anemia; early screening is essential.
How would you differentiate ROP from Coats disease on examination? — ROP shows plus disease and demarcation line; Coats has telangiectasia and exudates without prematurity.
Why is laser photocoagulation preferred over cryotherapy in most settings? — Laser provides precise ablation, less scarring, and is safer for the infant.
What red flag would prompt urgent referral for retinal detachment? — Rapid progression to stage 4/5 or presence of plus disease.
If a baby has severe anemia (Hb 7 g/dL) and ROP stage 2, what is the priority? — Transfuse to raise Hb >8 g/dL before considering laser.
Why might a pulse oximeter reading of 95% still be dangerous for ROP? — Intermittent hyperoxia spikes can occur; continuous monitoring and trend analysis are needed.
What is the role of wide‑field imaging in low‑resource settings? — It documents progression when ophthalmoscopy is difficult and aids tele‑consultation.
When is cryotherapy indicated? — When laser equipment is unavailable or the infant cannot tolerate laser; it is a backup option.

ai.subject: Paediatrics
ai.summary: ROP is a progressive retinal vasoproliferative disorder seen in preterm infants, driven by oxygen fluctuations and systemic illness. Early detection and timely laser or cryotherapy prevent blindness.

sections.p: ROP is a disorder of retinal vascular development in preterm infants, characterised by abnormal vessel proliferation and fibrosis. Diagnosis is clinical, using indirect ophthalmoscopy or wide‑field retinal imaging.

t.b: Assesses retinal vascularisation; normal: vessels reach ora serrata by 30–32 weeks GA. Abnormal: avascular areas, plus haemorrhages or fibrovascular proliferation.
Provides documentation for monitoring progression and guiding treatment when ophthalmoscopy is difficult.

sections.p: The International Classification of ROP (ICROP) stages 1–5, with zones I–III and plus disease. Stage 5 is retinal detachment.

t.b: Determines urgency of treatment; stages 3–5 with plus disease require intervention.
